safety.basis: Wants misdemeanors enforced and repeat offenders prosecuted, paired with treatment and housing.

local-control.basis: Would modify HB 1110's state multifamily zoning mandate and give school districts more authority over graduation standards.

reform.basis: Runs as an independent against party-line politics and proposes a 50% assessment on political contributions.

immigration.basis: Supports a state credential for qualifying undocumented residents and a warrant requirement for ICE transfers, excluding new arrivals and people with felonies.

experience.basis: First-time candidate with no elected experience.

tech.basis: Platform says Flock surveillance cameras raise 'legitimate privacy concerns' and need clear access rules: a single clear statement for data-privacy guardrails on surveillance tech (pole_b), without a broader regulatory agenda.

contests.office_does: One of two Washington State Representatives for the 47th District (Kent, Auburn, Covington and Maple Valley area of South King County), serving a two-year term writing state law and budgets.
contests.race_blurb: A rematch of 2024: Democratic incumbent and House Speaker Pro Tempore Chris Stearns faces Republican Ted Cooke, a software tester and longtime party officer. They differ on taxes, parental rights, gender policy, climate and density.

candidates.summary: Incumbent State Representative and House Speaker Pro Tempore; a Navajo attorney, former Auburn City Councilmember and former Washington State Gambling Commission chair.
highlights: Calls reproductive and gender-affirming care 'a human right' the Legislature must protect [S3]
Voted yes on ESSB 6346, the 2026 millionaires' tax that I-645 would repeal [S5]
Voted yes on ESHB 1296 (2025), the parental-rights amendments I-1 would undo [S6]
Sponsored a clean energy infrastructure bill (HB 1461) signed into law [S2]
Endorsed by Gov. Ferguson, Rep. Adam Smith, the mayors of Auburn, Kent and Covington, and Washington Conservation Action [S1]

taxes.basis: Voted for the 2026 tax on household income over $1 million; no separate campaign statement on taxes.

spending.basis: Runs on delivered investment in affordable housing and behavioral health, and pledges to 'fight for investments in families' including universal childcare.

housing.basis: Cites expanding affordable housing as a result and priority; served on the King County Affordable Housing Commission.

climate.basis: Sponsored clean energy infrastructure legislation and is endorsed by Washington Conservation Action; no stated carbon-pricing position.

social.basis: Repeatedly calls reproductive and gender-affirming care a human right, calls Dobbs 'unconscionable', and cites recognition by Pro-Choice Washington.

parental-rights.basis: Single record item: voted yes on ESHB 1296, which amended the I-2081 parental-rights law; no campaign statement on the topic.

tech.basis: Sponsored HB 1221 on data privacy and security, which passed the Senate.

experience.basis: Sitting House Speaker Pro Tempore and committee vice chair with bills signed into law; former city councilmember.

candidates.summary: Republican software tester and team lead from Covington, a precinct committee officer since 2009 and former King County GOP 2nd Vice Chair. He lost this seat to Stearns in 2024.
highlights: Would freeze new taxes, eliminate taxes on income, property and fuel, and audit every state office [S1]
Would 'restore full parental rights in education' and post school curricula online for parental review [S1][S4]
Pledges to 'uphold the biological definition of gender' [S1]
Would end cap-and-trade and lower or eliminate the gas tax [S4]
Prefers 'starter homes with yards over high-density apartments forced on us by Olympia' [S1]

taxes.basis: Would freeze all new taxes and eliminate income, property and fuel taxes, and wants the capital gains tax eliminated.

spending.basis: Would audit every state office and program, cut waste, and stop increases in government spending.

housing.basis: Would ease the Growth Management Act, streamline permitting and cut taxes to spur building, while opposing state-driven high-density apartments.

safety.basis: Public safety first; would let police act on reasonable suspicion rather than probable cause and keep 'anti-police' members off use-of-force review boards.

climate.basis: Would end cap-and-trade (the Climate Commitment Act's mechanism) and eliminate fuel taxes to cut energy costs.

local-control.basis: Opposes 'high-density apartments forced on us by Olympia', would ease the Growth Management Act, and would end legislative commissions.

social.basis: Pledges to 'uphold the biological definition of gender'; a single repeated pamphlet line, with no other gender or reproductive policy detail.

parental-rights.basis: Would 'restore full parental rights in education', give parents 'oversight of children and education', and post all curricula online for parental review.

experience.basis: Has never held public office; party officer and 2024 challenger.

contests.office_does: One of two Washington State Representatives for the 48th District (parts of Redmond, Bellevue and Kirkland plus the Points communities and Medina), serving two-year terms writing state law and budgets.
contests.race_blurb: Two Democrats: incumbent Amy Walen, who voted against the 2026 millionaires' tax, and Redmond City Councilmember Jessica Forsythe, backed by the district and county Democrats and the State Labor Council. Forsythe finished 17 votes ahead in the primary.

candidates.summary: State Representative since 2019, chair of Consumer Protection & Business, and former Kirkland mayor; describes herself as a "pragmatic governing Democrat who works across the aisle."
highlights: Voted no on ESSB 6346, the 2026 millionaires' tax, calling it unconstitutional and "not progressive enough" while backing a high-earners income tax in another form [S3][S4]
Prime sponsor of bills enabling commercial-to-housing conversions and limiting historic designations [S3]
Says reproductive options and gender-affirming care "are health care" [S3]
Cites banning ICE agents from wearing masks and sponsoring a bill removing citizenship requirements from most professional licenses [S1][S3]

experience.basis: Seven-year legislator and committee chair with an enacted bill record, plus ten years in Kirkland city government.

taxes.basis: Voted against the millionaires' tax and proposed returning most of its revenue through a sales-tax cut, but says she supports a high-earners income tax and a corporate income tax in place of B&O.

spending.basis: Stresses balanced budgets, the credit downgrade and homelessness-authority oversight, while proposing robust childcare funding and "borrow now" infrastructure investment.

housing.basis: Record emphasizes supply and deregulation (conversions, historic-designation limits, occupancy limits), alongside financing tools for public housing authorities.

local-control.basis: Says she carried cities' concerns on missing-middle policy; The Urbanist reports she voted against statewide middle-housing reform.

safety.basis: Combines police-guild endorsement and support for law enforcement training with gun restrictions, police accountability and crisis-response services.

climate.basis: Voted for the Climate Commitment Act and supports low-carbon fuel standards, alongside an all-sources clean-energy list including nuclear and hydrogen.

immigration.basis: Supported the ICE mask ban and limits on ICE entering schools and hospitals without a warrant; sponsored HB 1889 opening professional licenses to non-citizens.

social.basis: Explicit written support for abortion rights and gender-affirming care as insured health care and for self-determined gender identity; cites backfilling Planned Parenthood funding.

parental-rights.basis: Voted yes on ESHB 1296 and says schools have "an essential role" in comprehensive sexual health education and in protecting children "from unhealthy or abusive families."

candidates.summary: Redmond City Councilmember since 2020 and former Council President; small business owner, SEIU member and former Emerge WA executive director.
highlights: Won tenant protections and $7.5M for housing and human services on the Redmond council [S1]
Co-wrote Redmond's Climate Emergency Declaration [S3]
Pledges to fight for the 2SLGBTQIA+ community, immigrant rights and reproductive freedom [S4]
Endorsed by the 48th and King County Democrats, the State Labor Council and former Gov. Inslee [S1][S5]

experience.basis: Six years of municipal office but no state legislative record, challenging a seven-year incumbent.

housing.basis: Emphasizes deeply affordable housing and renter protections, with a call for more housing at all affordability levels.

climate.basis: Co-wrote a climate emergency declaration and net-zero plan; wants to shift debate from upfront costs to the costs of climate change.

safety.basis: Chaired Redmond's alternative crisis response subcommittee and added mental health professionals to the crisis response team.

spending.basis: Calls K-12 underfunded and wants to fully fund education and reduce reliance on local levies.

immigration.basis: Says she fought for immigrant communities and will fight for immigrant rights.

social.basis: Pledges to fight for the 2SLGBTQIA+ community and reproductive freedom; cites safeguarding reproductive rights.

contests.office_does: A State Representative writes and votes on Washington state law and the operating, capital, and transportation budgets, covering school funding, the tax structure, housing rules, and criminal-justice statutes.
contests.race_blurb: A 2024 rematch: Democratic incumbent Lisa Callan, Capital Budget vice chair since 2019, against Republican Patrick Peacock, an Army veteran and King County GOP vice chair. Callan won the King County primary count 57.7% to 42.3%.

candidates.summary: Incumbent since 2019 and Vice Chair of the House Capital Budget Committee; former Issaquah School Board director and Boeing engineer.
highlights: Voted for ESSB 6346, the 2026 tax on income over $1 million, and wants a tax code that "doesn't squeeze working people" [S1][S3]
Pledges to "defend reproductive freedom" [S1]
Voted for ESHB 1296 (2025), the law I-1 would undo [S4]

taxes.basis: Voted for the 2026 tax on income over $1 million and campaigns for a tax code that does not squeeze working people.

spending.basis: Campaigns on school funding, youth mental health, childcare and workforce housing investment.

housing.basis: Calls for workforce housing and is endorsed by the Housing Alliance; mechanism not specified.

climate.basis: Pledges to protect forests and clean air; endorsed by Sierra Club and Washington Conservation Action.

experience.basis: In office since 2019 with budget-committee leadership.

social.basis: States she will defend reproductive freedom and is endorsed by Planned Parenthood Alliance Advocates; no LGBTQ+ or sports position found.

parental-rights.basis: Voted for ESHB 1296 (2025), which amended the I-2081 parent and guardian rights list.

candidates.summary: Army counter-intelligence veteran, Boeing security specialist and King County GOP vice chair, running again on no state income tax and lower fuel taxes.
highlights: "No state income tax. Roll back fuel taxes" [S2]
Would cut red tape blocking new home construction [S2]
Endorsed by the 5th LD and King County Republicans [S1]

taxes.basis: Opposes a state income tax in both the pamphlet and on his site and wants fuel taxes rolled back.

housing.basis: Housing plan is to cut the red tape blocking new construction.

safety.basis: Back officers, hold repeat offenders accountable, restore safe streets.

climate.basis: Wants fuel taxes rolled back on cost grounds; no direct climate-policy statement.

experience.basis: Calls himself not a career politician and has not held public office, though he is a county party officer.

parental-rights.basis: Asks schools to respect parents as partners in their kids' education; no notification or opt-out specifics.

contests.office_does: The State Senator is the 30th District's single member of the Washington Senate, voting on state law and budgets and confirming gubernatorial appointments.
contests.race_blurb: Incumbent Democrat Claire Wilson, a former Federal Way School Board director, faces first-time Republican candidate Michael Rutland, a retired Air Force senior master sergeant. The race splits on taxes, school policy, and local control.

candidates.summary: Incumbent state senator and former Federal Way School Board director whose record centers on early learning, childcare, and K-12 funding.
highlights: Voted for ESSB 6346, the 2026 tax on income over $1 million, and says millionaires should pay their fair share to fund education [S3][S8]
Voted for ESHB 1296 (the 2025 amendments I-1 would undo) and co-sponsored SB 5599 (2023) on youth shelters and protected health care [S9][S11]
Endorsed by WEA-PAC, SEIU 775, and Planned Parenthood Alliance Advocates [S15][S16][S17]

taxes.basis: Voted for the 9.9% tax on income over $1 million and says she will support legislation making millionaires pay their fair share to fund schools.

spending.basis: Runs on landmark childcare and early-learning investments and says education is still critically underfunded.

housing.basis: Cites delivering public resources for affordable housing for low-income families and people leaving homelessness.

safety.basis: Pairs votes for police pay raises and training with funding for drug treatment and recovery.

climate.basis: Describes the clean-energy transition as an opportunity and supports transit to reduce air pollution; no specific carbon-policy position.

experience.basis: Sitting senator and former eight-year school board director, against a first-time candidate.

social.basis: Co-sponsored SB 5599 on youth access to gender-affirming and reproductive care, sponsored the LGBTQ Commission, and campaigns on reproductive rights.

parental-rights.basis: Voted for ESHB 1296 and sponsored district-selected comprehensive sexuality education, while describing her work as empowering parents' voice.

candidates.summary: First-time candidate, retired Air Force senior master sergeant and former Boeing manager, running on cost of living, opposition to new income taxes, and local control.

Calls for protecting local decision-making and reducing one-size-fits-all state mandates [S3]
Endorsed by the King County Republican Party and former 30th LD Senator Mark Miloscia [S4][S6]

taxes.basis: Repeatedly pledges to oppose new income taxes and calls for budgeting instead of higher taxes.

spending.basis: Calls for responsible budgeting and a government that lives within its means.

safety.basis: Supports law enforcement and addressing repeat offenses, while also listing prevention and intervention programs.

local-control.basis: Lists protecting local decision-making and reducing one-size-fits-all mandates as a priority.

experience.basis: First-time candidate with no elected experience, running against a sitting senator.

contests.office_does: The State Senator is the 31st District's single member of the Washington Senate, voting on state law and budgets and confirming gubernatorial appointments.

candidates.summary: Senator since 2017 and earlier a state representative, running on spending restraint, Second Amendment rights, and parental rights.

Proposes zero-based budgeting and funding transportation without raising taxes [S3]
Endorsed by the Association of Washington Business and the King County Republican Party [S12][S13]

experience.basis: Senator since 2017 with earlier House service, against a first-time candidate.

social.basis: Voted against ESSB 5599 on youth access to gender-affirming and reproductive care; no further statements found.

parental-rights.basis: Voted against ESHB 1296's amendments to the I-2081 parental-rights list and campaigns on defending parental rights.

candidates.summary: First-time candidate, Democratic precinct officer, and PTA and school-bond organizer from near Lake Tapps, running on infrastructure, school funding, and cost of living.

Would change the school funding model and expand free school meals to all schools [S3]
Would support laws prohibiting surveillance and surge pricing [S3]

social.basis: Endorsed by Planned Parenthood Alliance Advocates; no stated position on reproductive or LGBTQ+ policy.

climate.basis: Lists advancing renewable energy and green jobs and safeguarding the environment.

Endorsed by the Seattle Times (per his site), AWB and the Snohomish County Sheriff [S4][S14]

parental-rights.basis: Voted for ESHB 1296, the 2025 amendments to the I-2081 parental-rights list; no campaign statement on the topic.

tech.basis: Cites leading the fight to block AI-powered rent-setting schemes.

contests.office_does: One of 49 Washington State Senators, serving four-year terms writing state law and the state budget for the 36th District (Ballard, Magnolia, Queen Anne and the Greenwood area of northwest Seattle).

candidates.summary: State Senator since 2023 after seven years as the district's State Representative; Vice Chair of Finance on Ways & Means and a leading advocate of progressive tax restructuring.

Prime sponsor of wealth-tax bills since 2021 [S2][S4]
Cites expansion of the Working Families Tax Credit and senior property-tax exemption [S1]
Voted for ESHB 1296 (2025 parental-rights amendments) and EHB 1217 (2025 rent-increase limit) [S7][S8]

housing.basis: Voted for the 2025 rent-increase limit and cites 'historic investments in affordable housing.'

candidates.summary: Republican challenger, longtime precinct committee officer and 36th District Republican vice chair with a career in computer science and health-care operations; running to repeal the millionaires' tax and the Climate Commitment Act.

Would repeal the Climate Commitment Act and accelerate nuclear and natural gas [S1][S3]
Calls for clearing encampments and for 'exit' programs rather than housing alone [S1][S3]

taxes.basis: Top priority is repealing the millionaires' tax; also targets the sales and B&O taxes.

tech.basis: Calls Seattle's data-center moratorium 'Luddite symbolism' and wants to capture AI infrastructure growth.

social.basis: Campaign post calls sex 'binary' and gender-affirming interventions for minors 'elective and irreversible interventions that sterilize.'

parental-rights.basis: Says she will oppose any policy that 'weakens parental rights over minor children,' criticizes shelter notification going to DCYF instead of parents, and says schools should 'educate students rather than indoctrinate them.'

contests.office_does: One of 49 Washington State Senators, serving four-year terms writing state law and the state budget for the 37th District (southeast Seattle, Skyway and part of Renton).

Chipalo Street, who voted for the millionaires' tax and rent stabilization and has broad labor and party backing, and first-time candidate Tatiana Brown, an environmental-justice organizer who refuses corporate and PAC money. candidates.summary: State Representative since 2023 and Microsoft technologist, running for the open Senate seat with endorsements from the outgoing senator, the House Speaker, labor unions and the King County Democrats.
highlights: Voted for the 2026 millionaires' tax and campaigns on it [S1][S6]
Voted for the 2025 rent-increase limit and cites zoning reform to increase home building [S1][S8]

parental-rights.basis: Voted for ESHB 1296, which narrowed I-2081's parental notification and records rights; no public statements on the topic.

Calls for a statewide moratorium on new hyperscale AI data centers and making data centers pay for their energy use [S4]
Would formally refuse ICE cooperation and champion SB 5906 to 'ICE-proof' schools [S4][S5]

taxes.basis: Wants the wealthiest to pay their fair share; proposes new progressive revenue, closing the data-center sales-tax exemption and a higher top real-estate excise tax bracket.

spending.basis: Pledges to direct investments into the district and fully fund school counselors and social workers, and to defend college grants.

climate.basis: Co-chairs the Environmental Justice Council implementing the HEAL Act, helped shape CCA advocacy, and runs on climate justice.

experience.basis: First run for elected office; community-organizer profile against a sitting legislator.

reform.basis: Refuses corporate and PAC money and campaigns on government-funded community assemblies.

tech.basis: Calls for a statewide moratorium on new hyperscale AI data centers and for developers to pay for their energy use.

contests.office_does: One of 49 Washington State Senators, serving a four-year term writing state law, budgets and taxes for the 43rd District (Capitol Hill, University District, Wallingford, Fremont, Eastlake and downtown Seattle).
contests.race_blurb: Two Democrats: Senate Majority Leader Jamie Pedersen, prime sponsor of the 2026 millionaires tax that I-645 would repeal, faces labor communicator Hannah Sabio-Howell, who runs to his left and refuses corporate PAC money. candidates.summary: Senate Majority Leader, in the Legislature since 2007 and general counsel at McKinstry; prime sponsor of the 2026 tax on household income over $1 million.

Cites banning masked ICE agents and limiting camera surveillance for immigration enforcement [S1]
Leads on marriage equality, LGBTQ+ civil rights and transgender privacy protections; cites abortion rights [S1]
Says he worked to 'defend the Climate Commitment Act' and backed $100 million for police hiring and training [S4]
Voted for ESHB 1296 (2025); defended the millionaires tax against the repeal effort [S10][S7]

taxes.basis: Prime sponsor of the millionaires tax and the capital gains tax, but paired with tax cuts, with openness to estate-tax rollback and opposition to a payroll-tax fund.

spending.basis: Commits to 'amply funding schools' and cites $1.4 billion more for school districts and $770 million for housing.

housing.basis: Voted for 2025 rent stabilization and cites housing funding, alongside laws streamlining housing construction.

safety.basis: Supported a $100 million police hiring and training investment, alongside license-revocation reform for misconduct.

climate.basis: Says he worked to defend the Climate Commitment Act; cites climate action among accomplishments.

experience.basis: In the Legislature since 2007, Senate Majority Leader, with an enacted signature tax law.

local-control.basis: Voted for ESHB 2266, a state requirement that cities allow supportive housing and shelters in specified zones.

reform.basis: Frames his approach as coalition-building; accepts institutional and union backing and holds a large fundraising lead, against a no-corporate-PAC opponent.

immigration.basis: Cites enacted bans on masked ICE agents and on camera surveillance for immigration enforcement.

social.basis: Long record leading on marriage equality, LGBTQ+ civil rights and transgender privacy; cites abortion rights and Planned Parenthood funding.

parental-rights.basis: Voted yea on ESHB 1296 (2025), which amended the I-2081 parents' rights law; no statement on the topic.

'The only campaign in this race not taking corporate PAC money' [S1]
Would restrict AI and surveillance use by law enforcement, 'including the expansion of data centers' [S4]
No public position found on the three initiatives [S3][S4][S5]

taxes.basis: Wants a corporate income tax, a payroll-based fund and reversal of tax cuts for the ultra-wealthy, beyond the millionaires tax.

spending.basis: Proposes universal pre-K, a home-care cash benefit, restored childcare enrollment and social housing investment.

housing.basis: Social housing investment and a tighter rent cap, paired with statewide supply deregulation ('ending apartment bans', cutting red tape).

safety.basis: Non-police responders for non-violent calls, community programs as alternatives to incarceration, restoring use-of-force standards.

experience.basis: No elected office; runs against 'career politicians who protect the status quo'.

local-control.basis: Wants to end apartment bans statewide and build housing 'everywhere', plus a tighter statewide rent cap.

reform.basis: Refuses corporate PAC money, frames the race against corporate deal-making, and supports even-year local elections.

immigration.basis: Would shield data from immigration enforcement, strip incentives from ICE contractors and bar hiring former ICE officers.

healthcare.basis: Supports the state backstopping federal cuts and taking steps toward universal healthcare.

social.basis: Serves on the Pro-Choice Washington PAC board 'to advance reproductive justice'; organized with queer rights organizations.

tech.basis: Would regulate and restrict AI and surveillance use by law enforcement, including the expansion of data centers.

contests.office_does: One of 49 Washington State Senators, serving a four-year term writing state law and budgets for the 46th District in northeast Seattle.
contests.race_blurb: Incumbent Democrat Javier Valdez, a Senate committee chair, faces Republican Sandra Stephens, a retired nurse in her first campaign. Valdez won about 91% of the primary vote.

candidates.summary: Incumbent State Senator and chair of the Senate State Government, Tribal Affairs and Elections Committee; in the Legislature since 2017, first in the House.
highlights: Prime sponsor of SB 5855 (2026), banning face-concealing masks for law enforcement including ICE agents; final Senate approval March 9, 2026 [S6]
Voted yes on ESSB 6346 (2026), the tax on household income over $1 million that I-645 would repeal [S9]
Voted yes on ESHB 1296 (2025), the parents' rights amendments that I-1 would undo [S8]
Says he helped backfill Planned Parenthood funding and supported a cap on rent increases [S1]

taxes.basis: Voted for ESSB 6346, the millionaires' income tax, and campaigns on having voted to tax millionaires and the very wealthy.

spending.basis: Frames new revenue as paying for free school lunches, small-business tax relief and healthcare investments.

housing.basis: Cites a cap on rent increases alongside zoning reform for more affordable housing.

immigration.basis: Prime sponsor of SB 5855 banning masked ICE and police officers; says he barred federal camera surveillance of immigrants.

social.basis: Says he helped backfill state Planned Parenthood funding after federal cuts; endorsed by Planned Parenthood Alliance Advocates.

parental-rights.basis: Voted yes on ESHB 1296 (2025), which amended the I-2081 parents' rights law; single vote, no campaign statement on the topic.

experience.basis: In the Legislature since 2017, Senate committee chair, with an enacted record.

candidates.summary: Retired registered nurse and first-time candidate endorsed by the King County Republican Party; her statement centers on alleged corruption and the pro-life position.
highlights: States a belief in 'the sacredness of life'; two terms in the National Association of Pro-Life Nurses (1988-1992) [S1]
Attributes rising taxes and declining services to 'theft of taxpayers funds through unaudited nonprofits' [S1]
Says the King County Republican Party platform represents her policies [S1]

social.basis: States belief in 'the sacredness of life' and served in a pro-life nurses' association.

spending.basis: Centers her statement on unaudited nonprofit funding and misuse of taxpayer money, an audit-first framing.

experience.basis: First-time candidate with no public-office record; background is nursing and volunteering.

contests.office_does: One of 49 Washington State Senators, serving a four-year term writing state law and budgets for the 47th District (Kent, Auburn and Covington area of South King County).
contests.race_blurb: Incumbent Democrat Claudia Kauffman faces Republican Covington City Councilmember Kristina Soltys. Both talk about affordability and public safety; they split on income taxes, housing policy tools, and state versus local control.

candidates.summary: Incumbent State Senator since 2022, who also held the seat from 2007 to 2011; former Muckleshoot Tribe intergovernmental affairs liaison. Running on affordability, housing supply with renter protections, and the safety net.
highlights: Voted yes on ESSB 6346, the 2026 tax on household income over $1 million that I-645 would repeal [S5]
Platform says the bottom 20% pay 'SEVEN times more of their income in taxes than billionaires' and proposes cutting property and sales taxes [S4]
Wants more housing supply and protection for renters from 'predatory price gouging' [S1]
Voted yes on ESHB 1296 (2025), the parental-rights amendments I-1 would undo [S6]
Endorsed by Gov. Ferguson, the mayors of Auburn, Covington and Kent, the State Labor Council and Washington Conservation Action [S1][S3][S11]

taxes.basis: Voted for the 2026 millionaires' tax (ESSB 6346) and argues the tax code burdens the poor far more than billionaires, proposing lower sales and property taxes instead.

spending.basis: Emphasizes expanded childcare, a 'robust' safety net and capital investments, without a stated program to expand public spending broadly.

housing.basis: Pairs housing supply with renter protections against 'predatory price gouging' and middle-income housing.

parental-rights.basis: Single record item: voted yes on ESHB 1296, which amended the I-2081 parental-rights law; no campaign statement on the topic.

experience.basis: Two Senate stints (2007-2011, 2022-present), committee leadership, and a 2026 legislative record.

candidates.summary: Covington City Councilmember since 2019 and former diagnostic medical sonographer who immigrated from Ukraine as a child. Running against the income tax and recent tax increases, and for permitting reform and police funding.
highlights: Opposes a state income tax ('Washington voters have rejected an income tax ten times') and says Olympia has 'a spending problem' [S4]
Said in July of the income tax repeal effort that an income tax 'doesn't belong here' [S5]
Favors permitting reform and market incentives; says state government should empower local communities rather than impose mandates [S4]
On the council: funded an additional police officer and started a community resource officer program for residents in crisis [S1]
Has raised more than the incumbent: $208.9K in contributions [S6]

taxes.basis: Repeated opposition to an income tax and to recent B&O and gas tax increases; calls the state's problem one of spending, not revenue.

spending.basis: 'Spending problem' framing and demand for budget results, while also backing funding for police and transportation.

housing.basis: Relies on permitting reform and market incentives over state mandates; no tenant-protection or public-housing proposals.

local-control.basis: 'Local communities know their neighborhoods. State government should empower them'; opposes top-down mandates, stated for housing.

safety.basis: Prioritizes fully funded police and more officers, paired with treatment resources and a community resource officer program.

experience.basis: Seven years on a city council but new to the Legislature, running against a long-serving incumbent.
